flow.costPlain: Running Snowflake's platform — data centers and the cost of delivering its product and services.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Sales teams and marketing. Up 14% YoY — growing, but slower than revenue.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Building the platform and its AI products. Up 15% YoY; includes $231M of stock-based pay.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: The back office — finance, legal and admin. Up 125% YoY, lifted by a $106M office-exit impairment charge.

follow100Note: Snowflake spent $142.91 of every $100 it took in on direct and running costs — more than it earned — and other income added $2.21 while tax took $0.55, leaving a $41.26 loss per $100. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Snowflake reports in thousands (revenue was $1,042,074K); figures here are shown in $M to three decimals so the lines foot exactly. Excluding stock-based pay and other non-GAAP items, operating income was $92M (a 9% margin). Chart note: Snowflake's running costs exceeded its gross profit by $447M and other income covered $23M of that, so the chart draws the remaining $430M net loss as a 'Covered by cash on hand' source, which also covers the $5.7M tax bill.
oneTimers: A $106.5M impairment charge for exiting Snowflake's San Mateo office — the office was ceased using during the quarter — booked inside general and administrative expense and excluded from non-GAAP results along with stock-based pay and other items.
otherDetail: Other income of $23M, net: $53M of interest income on Snowflake's cash and investments, less $2M of interest expense and $28M of other expense, net. Net loss attributable to Snowflake Inc. was $430M (EPS -$1.29), after $0.1M of income attributable to noncontrolling interests.

segments.name: Product
segments.note: Customers pay to store data and run computing and AI workloads on Snowflake's platform, billed by how much they use. Up 26% YoY and 96% of all revenue.

segments.name: Professional services and other
segments.note: Help getting set up and moving data onto Snowflake, plus other small items. Up 16% YoY — but it costs more to deliver than it brings in (an $18.2M gross loss).

takeaways.text: Product revenue rose 26% to $997M, the net revenue retention rate was 124%, and remaining performance obligations — work customers have already contracted — grew 34% to $6.7B. Snowflake also guided Q2 product revenue to $1,035–$1,040M, up 25%, and full-year FY26 product revenue to $4,325M, up 25%.
takeaways.title: Product growth stayed strong

takeaways.text: The GAAP operating loss was $447M. The main reasons: $409M of stock-based compensation-related charges and a $106M impairment for exiting the San Mateo office. Leaving those and similar items out, non-GAAP operating income was $92M, a 9% margin.
takeaways.title: Still a GAAP loss, mostly stock pay and an office exit

takeaways.text: Snowflake ended the quarter with 606 customers spending over $1M a year on the platform (+27% YoY) and 754 Forbes Global 2000 customers. Operating cash flow was $228M and adjusted free cash flow was $206M.
takeaways.title: Big customers kept spending

verdict: Snowflake's revenue grew 26% to $1.04B, with product revenue up 26% to $997M — but $409M of stock-based pay and a $106M office-exit impairment helped leave a GAAP operating loss of $447M and a net loss of $430M.
